description:
## Problem
BenchBox's generator is unverified against the reference. DIGen and PDGF cannot be shipped, but a user may run their own copy.

## Owner decisions (choice dialogs, 2026-11-20)
- "Before the milestone, you supply DIGen once on this machine and I run the same ETL and audit on DIGen data at the smallest scale and compare row counts per file; nothing from DIGen is committed."
- "BenchBox answers DIGen's prompt only with an explicit `--accept-tpcdi-tools-license` (recorded in the bundle); Java is found through `JAVA_HOME` then `PATH`; absent or unsupported Java fails with instructions; BenchBox never downloads Java. A DIGen-sourced result is not publishable on benchbox.dev until you have settled the PDGF use clause."

## Change
New benchbox/core/tpcdi/digen.py: locate a user-supplied DIGen directory (config key and option shown to the owner), find Java, run DIGen through the run deadline with no fixed timeout, answer the licence prompt only with the opt-in flag, verify the three batch directories and the report, parse row counts. Mark any DIGen-sourced result non-publishable. Then run the comparison: generate scale 3 with DIGen and with sourcegen, load both through step 12's ETL and audit, and report per-file row counts and audit outcomes side by side.

## Clean-room rule (owner: "Strict clean room: the implementer reads only the specification, the paper and the TPC appendix SQL.")
The implementer reads only the TPC-DI v1.1.0 specification, the VLDB 2014 paper (Poess, Rabl, Jacobsen, Caufield) and the TPC appendix SQL. It never opens PDGF configuration or dictionaries, DIGen or PDGF source or decompiled classes, the `tpc-di_src.jar` plugin source, or `shannon-barrow/databricks-tpc-di`'s `tpcdi_gen`. Subagents get the same rule in their brief. The pull request description states that the rule was followed.

## Decision gates
Owner action first: the owner extracts DIGen from the archive on this machine and names the directory; blocked until then. The implementer treats DIGen as a black box: it runs it and reads its OUTPUT files and report, and opens no file under the PDGF directory and no DIGen source (clean-room rule). The option and config key names are shown to the owner before commit. The supported Java versions are set from what actually runs here and reported. DIGen's known wrong answer key for C_DOB_TO and C_DOB_TY applies only to batches 2 and 3; if the Batch 1 audit fails on DIGen data, report it as a finding about BenchBox's ETL, do not adjust the audit.

## Verification rubric
Pass: unit tests with the subprocess mocked cover absent Java, unsupported Java, missing flag (refusal that prints the licence location), and the publish refusal; the comparison table (file, DIGen rows, sourcegen rows, ratio; audit tests OK on each) is recorded on this item and in the pull request; no file from the archive or DIGen output is in the diff (`git diff --stat` shows only BenchBox code and tests); `make pr-preflight` passes.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
- The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`.
- Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking. `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job the runner never ran or cancelled, never for a failed test.
- Review threads: reply; resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again.
- Subagents are read-only. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment.
- Any limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has not already chosen (see tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120) is shown to the owner before it is committed.
- A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`. One pull request for this item, merged before the next item starts.
- From the quarantine step until the reopening step, no TPC-DI entry point may produce a result that reads PASSED or is admitted for publication.
